Beyoncé was the big winner at Sunday night’s 67th [Grammy Awards](https://deadline.com/tag/grammy-awards/).
For the first time ever, the _Cowboy Carter_ artist won the award for Album of the Year, beating out Charli XCX, Jacob Collier, Billie Eilish, Chappell Roan, Taylor Swift, André 300 and Sabrina Carpenter.

### Album release
On March 19, 2024, Beyoncé revealed the album cover via Instagram, and said there would be "surprises" and collaborations on the album.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-pitchfork1-66) On March 20, she revealed a limited edition exclusive cover, wearing a sash that reads "act ii BEYINCÉ", referencing the generational family surname of her mother, [Tina Knowles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tina_Knowles "Tina Knowles").[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-67)[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-68) Taglines and [film stills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Film_stills "Film stills") for the album were projected onto various museums in New York City.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-69) One was an unauthorized projection onto the [Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solomon_R._Guggenheim_Museum "Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum"), which responded good-naturedly by posting [Franz Marc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franz_Marc "Franz Marc")'s 1910 painting _Three Horses Drinking_ with the caption "This ain't Texas" in reference to "Texas Hold 'Em".[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-70) Beyoncé also posted [co-ordinates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spatial_reference_system "Spatial reference system") to the museum on her [Instagram story](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Instagram_story "Instagram story").[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-71)
